title: Recipe 22 — Compliance and Audit (the hash chain is the evidence)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “SOC 2 evidence out of the audit log you already have — not a screenshot of a dashboard.”
beats.script: SOC 2 evidence out of the audit log you already have — not a screenshot of a dashboard. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens 22 compliance and audit.md now. Keep this artifact in view: it is the concrete evidence behind the behavior this beat describes.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take.
beats.script: Live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash crewhaus.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env into this one terminal.
beats.script: Sources demos/.env into this one terminal. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Operator-supplied demos/.env.

beats.label: Type recipe 11's managed harness
beats.cue: “Audit is a property of the managed multitenant shape — so start from that starter, unchanged. Two tenants, two budgets.”
beats.script: Audit is a property of the managed multitenant shape — so start from that starter, unchanged. Two tenants, two budgets. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 1 through 15 of starters slash managed slash crewhaus.yaml, rebuilding live slash crewhaus.yaml from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean before we ask it for evidence — so anything the collector says later is about the log, not the spec.”
beats.script: Clean before we ask it for evidence — so anything the collector says later is about the log, not the spec. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Lint: clean — no findings.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The tenant list is spec sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually lowers it to.”
beats.script: The tenant list is spec sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually lowers it to. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Prints the IR for target managed.

verify.note: prints the IR for target managed

beats.label: Compile the bundle
beats.cue: “The audit trail is emitted code, not a service you trust — here it is, compiled. The managed daemon is scaffolding; recipe 11 is where its boot gets proved.”
beats.script: The audit trail is emitted code, not a service you trust — here it is, compiled. The managed daemon is scaffolding; recipe 11 is where its boot gets proved. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Emits the daemon bundle. Deliberately not --check: a managed daemon binds :3000, and --check scrubs the environment (so PORT cannot be overridden), which means exactly one driver in the suite may boot one — that is recipe 11's.

verify.note: emits the daemon bundle. Deliberately not --check: a managed daemon binds :3000, and --check scrubs the environment (so PORT cannot be overridden), which means exactly one driver in the suite may boot one — that is recipe 11's.

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “The daemon that writes the audit log. You own this file — it is not behind a framework.”
beats.script: The daemon that writes the audit log. You own this file — it is not behind a framework. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens live slash dist slash daemon.ts now. The relevant implementation is now visible, so the claim can be inspected directly instead of taken on faith.

groups.title: Beat 3 · the hash chain, and what breaks it

beats.label: Verify an empty chain
beats.cue: “Nothing has served a request yet, so the chain is empty — and it still tells you the limitation: with no anchor, tail truncation cannot be ruled out.”
beats.script: Nothing has served a request yet, so the chain is empty — and it still tells you the limitation: with no anchor, tail truncation cannot be ruled out. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. ✓ hash chain intact — 0 record(s) checked; ~ on-host chain-tail anchor absent (limitation, not tamper).

verify.note: ✓ hash chain intact — 0 record(s) checked; ~ on-host chain-tail anchor absent (limitation, not tamper)

beats.label: Make room for a forged chain
beats.cue: “Now the other half of the claim — what does the verifier do with a chain it did not write?”
beats.script: Now the other half of the claim — what does the verifier do with a chain it did not write? [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash forged slash chain.jsonl in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Type the recipe's illustrative chain
beats.cue: “The recipe's own three sample records, verbatim — with the hashes elided to abc1, def4, 0234.”
beats.script: The recipe's own three sample records, verbatim — with the hashes elided to abc1, def4, 0234. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 48 through 50 of 22 compliance and audit.md, rebuilding live slash forged slash chain.jsonl from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Verify the forged chain — it refuses
beats.cue: “Exit 1, with the line number and both hashes: expected the real SHA-256, got abc1. A hash that does not commit to the body is not evidence.”
beats.script: Exit 1, with the line number and both hashes: expected the real SHA-256, got abc1. A hash that does not commit to the body is not evidence. [[pause:1.5s]] Do not treat this rejection as a broken demo; exit code 1 is the expected outcome. Deliberate rejection exit 1: tamper finding at chain.jsonl:1, hash mismatch. The recipe's sample hashes are elided placeholders, so the verifier rejects them.

verify.note: deliberate rejection — exit 1: tamper finding at chain.jsonl:1, hash mismatch. The recipe's sample hashes are elided placeholders, so the verifier rejects them — which is exactly its "a broken link is proof of tampering", proved offline.

beats.label: Collect a quarter of SOC 2 evidence
beats.cue: “Every SOC 2 control, queried against the log, one bundle per control. Four files, no auditor spreadsheet.”
beats.script: Every SOC 2 control, queried against the log, one bundle per control. Four files, no auditor spreadsheet. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. Writes .crewhaus/compliance/soc2/{CC6.1,CC6.7,CC7.2,CC7.3}/2026-Q2.json; warns "evidence gap — 4 control(s) collected 0 records" because this scratch harness has never served a request.

verify.note: writes .crewhaus/compliance/soc2/{CC6.1,CC6.7,CC7.2,CC7.3}/2026-Q2.json; warns "evidence gap — 4 control(s) collected 0 records" because this scratch harness has never served a request

beats.label: Open the CC6.7 bundle
beats.cue: “frameworkId, controlId, period, recordCount, records, digest, signature — self-verifying, and verifyBundle re-checks every one of those before an auditor trusts it.”
beats.script: FrameworkId, controlId, period, recordCount, records, digest, signature — self-verifying, and verifyBundle re-checks every one of those before an auditor trusts it. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens .crewhaus slash compliance slash soc2 slash CC6.7 slash 2026 Q2.json now. Keep this artifact in view: it is the concrete evidence behind the behavior this beat describes.

beats.label: Make the evidence gap fail the job
beats.cue: “Zero records for a control is the finding, not the absence of one. --fail-on-empty turns that warning into exit 1 — that is your quarterly cron.”
beats.script: Zero records for a control is the finding, not the absence of one. --fail-on-empty turns that warning into exit 1 — that is your quarterly cron. [[pause:1.5s]] The refusal is the proof in this beat, so the verifier expects exit code 1. Deliberate non-zero — exit 1: "evidence gap — 4 control(s) collected 0 records for 2026-Q2 (--fail-on-empty)".

verify.note: deliberate non-zero — exit 1: "evidence gap — 4 control(s) collected 0 records for 2026-Q2 (--fail-on-empty)"

beats.label: Try to escape the output directory
beats.cue: “Framework, control and period are validated as identifiers, so a buggy CI script cannot talk the collector into overwriting an unrelated file.”
beats.script: Framework, control and period are validated as identifiers, so a buggy CI script cannot talk the collector into overwriting an unrelated file. [[pause:1.5s]] The refusal is the proof in this beat, so the verifier expects exit code 1. Deliberate rejection — exit 1: framework name must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/ (the recipe's path-traversal refusal section).

verify.note: deliberate rejection — exit 1: framework name must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/ (the recipe's path-traversal refusal section)

groups.title: One more thing · retention is audited too

beats.cue: “A real sweep — not a dry run — appends its own record. Retention enforcement is itself tamper-evidenced.”
beats.script: A real sweep — not a dry run — appends its own record. Retention enforcement is itself tamper-evidenced. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. 0 deleted, 0 kept — evidence appended to .crewhaus/audit (seq 0).

beats.label: Verify the chain again
beats.cue: “One record now, and the on-host anchor matches the surviving tail. That is the difference between a log and evidence.”
beats.script: One record now, and the on-host anchor matches the surviving tail. That is the difference between a log and evidence.
